topic.title: Why the casino always wins, even when you win

title: How the casino wins even on your lucky night 🎰
description:
If you can win at roulette, how does the casino always come out ahead?
The house edge on a double-zero roulette wheel (5.26%) on every $10 bet, added up over an hour, a night, a year of Saturdays and ten years of them: on average, computed. Speak to a licensed financial adviser in your country before making financial decisions.
An animated story with illustrative numbers; the characters are not advisers.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: Ever left a casino richer? Comment

lines.text: The casino never gambles. It wins a slice of every bet.
Let's follow Rohan's chips through four levels. The last one takes a whole decade.
See the green zeros on the wheel? When the ball lands there, every red and black bet loses. That's my edge: 5.26%, on average.
Level one. I bet $10 a spin for an hour. On average, the house keeps $20.
Level two, a whole night of spins. The same few chips, bet over and over. That's $100 to the house.
Level three: every Saturday for a year. The house collects $5,197, one little slice at a time.
Level four: 10 years of Saturdays. On average, $51,969 of Rohan's money, slipped into my casino.
Hold on. Last Saturday I won! I walked out with a trophy and a free drink.
And I love that night. A win is what brings him back next Saturday. The edge never sleeps.
So the casino doesn't need luck. It just needs players who keep coming back.
Still, one more spin couldn't hurt. Right?
